claim_statement: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.

plan.claim: OT loss and refinement efficacy: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2. Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
plan.hypothesis: On synthetic Gaussian point sets, Monte Carlo Sliced Wasserstein (proxy for Eq.10/11 BiSW/BiEBSW LOT loss, O(L n log n) time O(n) memory) will show lower median wall-clock runtime and more favorable descriptive runtime growth with n than entropy-regularized Sinkhorn (proxy for Eq.14 adaptive refinement, O(n^2) memory O(n^2*iters) time) when both are run CPU-only on identical data with fixed seeds, dim=32, L=64 projections, sinkhorn_reg=0.05 max_iter=100 tol=1e-6, 5 timed reps plus 2 warmup reps, reporting runtime DISTRIBUTIONS median/IQR never single timing as proof. This tests ONLY computational cost scaling, NOT correspondence accuracy.

dependent_vars: runtime_s: Wall-clock seconds per OT distance computation per rep after warmup, reported as full distribution median IQR mean std min max over reps, primary comparison uses median
distance_value: Scalar OT estimate sliced mean 1D Wasserstein vs Sinkhorn entropic cost used ONLY for numerical sanity finite non-negative no NaN Inf NOT for accuracy since objectives differ
sinkhorn_iters_to_tol: Actual Sinkhorn iterations executed until tol or max_iter for convergence sanity
controlled_vars: feature_dim: Ambient dimension dim=32 fixed for all n
sampling_distribution: I.i.d. Gaussian N(0,I_d) synthetic clouds with fixed seeds no mesh structure no FAUST SCAPE SHREC19 geometry
n_projections_L: Number of random slicing directions for SW L=64 fixed directions uniform on S^{d-1} per rep via fixed seeds
sinkhorn_regularization: Entropic regularization sinkhorn_reg=0.05 fixed defines different objective from SW
sinkhorn_max_iter_and_tol: Max iterations 100 and stopping tolerance 1e-6 on marginal violation documented and fixed
repetitions_and_seeds: Fixed seeds [0,1,2,3,4] reps=5 plus warmup_reps=2 per (n,algorithm) not counted single-threaded CPU no GPU BLAS threads=1 if configurable
hardware_provenance: Must log CPU model RAM OS Python numpy scipy versions thread settings and report median IQR provenance for every cell
algorithms: sliced_wasserstein: Monte Carlo Sliced Wasserstein draw L=64 unit vectors project X Y sort each projection O(n log n) compute 1D Wasserstein via sorted differences average over L O(L n log n) time O(n) memory CPU numpy sort proxy for Eq.4/5/10/11

sinkhorn: Entropic-regularized OT via Sinkhorn-Knopp on dense n x n squared Euclidean cost matrix O(n^2) memory O(n^2*iters) time iters<=100 eps=0.05 tol=1e-6 CPU numpy scipy proxy for Eq.3/14 adaptive refinement

budget.note: Cost-aware estimate BEFORE choosing sizes: Sinkhorn O(n^2*iters) memory/time dominates. At max_n=2048 n^2=4.19M floats ~33MB per cost matrix 100 iters ~419M ops per call ~0.2-0.5s CPU. Sliced O(L n log n) ~0.005-0.02s per call. With 4 sizes*2 algs*(5+2 reps)=56 calls: sinkhorn 28*~0.3s=8.4s sliced 28*~0.01s=0.3s plus overhead ~30-60s total well within 10-min sandbox designed for ~3 min cheap max_n capped at 2048 to avoid quadratic OOM

limitations: Requires licensed/registered 3D human shape meshes: FAUST (~100 scans) + SCAPE (71 meshes) for training with specific remeshing, and SHREC19 (430 pairs) for testing, plus pretrained DiffusionNet weights and full unsupervised FM+OT joint training pipeline to reproduce Table 4 ablation. No synthetic data can yield the claimed geodesic errors.
Synthetic Gaussian point clouds in R^32 have no mesh topology isometry or part semantics; no functional maps, DiffusionNet features, or segmentation transfer evaluated.

Sliced Wasserstein and entropy-regularized OT are DIFFERENT objectives with different regularization and metric properties (SW valid metric, Sinkhorn not triangle inequality); runtime differences say nothing about accuracy or the 4.7 to 7.2 MSE/refinement degradation claim.

Results are descriptive runtime scaling on one CPU/software stack with eps=0.05 tol=1e-6 max_iter=100, not a proof of O(n log n) vs O(n^2) asymptotic complexity; do not claim proven complexity from few sizes.
Quadratic Sinkhorn baseline capped at max_n=2048 to avoid O(n^2) memory/time blowup; operating point fixed, not tuned training regime.
plan.scope_notes: Scope: SW vs entropic-OT runtime scaling on synthetic point sets ONLY. Keep cheap: at most 4 sizes max_n<=2048 at most 2 algorithms sliced_wasserstein sinkhorn reps<=5 projections<=128 Sinkhorn iters<=200 total ~3 min. This experiment does NOT test correspondence accuracy geodesic error MSE vs LOT degradation or refinement efficacy on real shapes and does NOT reproduce Table 4 p.8 Sec.6 which requires FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19 and full unsupervised training. Hardware/runtime provenance expectations: report CPU model/cores RAM OS Python/numpy/scipy versions BLAS thread limit OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 no GPU fixed seeds warmup policy and present runtime DISTRIBUTIONS median+IQR+mean/std over reps for every (n,algorithm) cell. Numerical sanity checks required: assert all distances finite >=0 no overflow NaN Sinkhorn marginal error logged. Scaling interpretation: compare observed median runtime growth descriptively without claiming proven asymptotic complexity. Sliced Wasserstein and entropy-regularized OT are DIFFERENT objectives measuring one's runtime says nothing about the other's accuracy.

testability.rationale: Verifying the numeric ablation (MSE >> LOT, 4.7->7.2 without refinement) requires full unsupervised training of DiffusionNet feature extractor + Functional Map solver jointly with BiSW/BiEBSW OT loss on FAUST+SCAPE meshes and entropic Sinkhorn adaptive refinement inference on SHREC19, then computing mean geodesic error. This is GPU-heavy, multi-epoch training (hours/days), mesh-dependent, and cannot be reproduced on synthetic data on CPU in <10min. A synthetic proxy can only test directional alignment tendency, not the reported SHREC19 numbers or necessity claim.
testability.suggested_benchmark: Proxy synthetic distribution-alignment benchmark (CPU <10min): generate 50 paired synthetic point clouds n=256-512, d=16-32 from Gaussian mixtures with known permutation + non-isometric warp/noise; create soft similarity matrix via row-softmax of random/Shallow-MLP features (Eq9). Compute Bidirectional SW (Monte Carlo L=32-64, Eq10) and BiEBSW (importance-weighted, Eq11) vs MSE (Frobenius on similarities) loss values, gradients and resulting hard-map accuracy/Chamfer error. Separately run entropic Sinkhorn refinement (Eq14, 10 iterations) vs no-refinement/nearest-neighbor and measure error reduction and time/memory. Tests if SW/EBSW > MSE directionally, but does not reproduce SHREC19 4.7->7.2.
testability.unavailable_detail: Requires licensed/registered 3D human shape meshes: FAUST (~100 scans) + SCAPE (71 meshes) for training with specific remeshing, and SHREC19 (430 pairs) for testing, plus pretrained DiffusionNet weights and full unsupervised FM+OT joint training pipeline to reproduce Table 4 ablation. No synthetic data can yield the claimed geodesic errors.
